title: CRAX: Fast Safe Reinforcement Learning Benchmarking
statement: Every task is built so that high reward requires incurring cost.
quote: Each task defines reward and cost signals, inducing a trade-off between performance and safety: achieving high reward typically requires incurring higher cost, while satisfying safety constraints necessitates sacrificing some reward.

title: CRAX: Fast Safe Reinforcement Learning Benchmarking
statement: Tighter budgets force PPO-Lagrangian to give up reward in every task.
environment: CRAX Level tasks with d in {15;25;35}
quote: PPOLag increasingly sacrifices rewards to adhere to tighter safety bounds in all tasks.

title: CRAX: Fast Safe Reinforcement Learning Benchmarking
statement: At the hardest level exploration is swamped by violations so no good policy is found.
quote: when trained directly on the hardest difficulty level, agents often struggle to discover a good policy, as exploration becomes dominated by constraint violations and sparse progress.

title: CRAX: Fast Safe Reinforcement Learning Benchmarking
statement: Direct training leaves budget unused; transfer helps; the opposite holds in Safe Goal.
environment: CRAX Safe Pathway and Safe Height Level 3
quote: Here, direct training yields overly conservative policies that underutilize the available safety budget, while safety-transferred agents make better use of it.

title: CRAX: Fast Safe Reinforcement Learning Benchmarking
statement: PPO-Lagrangian satisfies all bounds at Levels 2-3 but earns low reward.
quote: PPOLag achieves the highest safety percentage, being the only baseline to satisfy all cost bounds on Levels 2 and 3. However, it fails to reach high rewards.

title: CRAX: Fast Safe Reinforcement Learning Benchmarking
statement: The reward-budget trade-off is non-linear; tightening hurts more than loosening helps.
quote: Tightening the bound leads to a substantially larger drop in score than the gains obtained by increasing it by the same amount.

title: CRAX: Fast Safe Reinforcement Learning Benchmarking
statement: Method success depends on the kind of constraint; Saute works only on some.
quote: PPOSauté satisfies the cost bound in Reacher and Pathway but otherwise behaves close to unconstrained PPO.

title: HASARD: A Benchmark for Vision-Based Safe Reinforcement Learning in Embodied Agents
statement: Reward and cost are designed to be tightly coupled so cost reduction costs reward.

title: Responsive Safety in Reinforcement Learning by PID Lagrangian Methods
statement: Gradient-ascent Lagrange multiplier oscillates with cost and overshoots the limit during training.
environment: Safety Gym DoggoButton1 (cost limit 200) and others
quote: Cost overshoot and oscillations are in fact inherent to the learning dynamics (Platt & Barr, 1988; Wah et al., 2000), and we witnessed numerous problematic cases in our own experiments.

title: Responsive Safety in Reinforcement Learning by PID Lagrangian Methods
statement: The multiplier is updated slowly so the penalty lags behind constraint-violating policies.
quote: Convergence proofs have relied upon updating the multiplier more slowly than the policy parameters (Tessler et al., 2018; Paternain et al., 2019), implying many constraint-violating policy iterations may occur before the penalty comes into full effect.

title: Responsive Safety in Reinforcement Learning by PID Lagrangian Methods
statement: Cost pressure from reward learning is nonstationary so λ needs to respond dynamically.
quote: As the agent learns for rewards, the upward pressure on costs from reward-learning can change, requiring dynamic response.

title: Safety-Gymnasium: A Unified Safe Reinforcement Learning Benchmark
statement: Lagrangian methods oscillate around the cost limit more than projection methods.

title: AutoCost: Evolving Intrinsic Cost for Zero-violation Reinforcement Learning
statement: He, Zhao and Liu (AAAI 2023) report that CPO and PPO-Lagrangian stay around the threshold and fail to reach zero violation even with a zero cost limit.
quote: CPO and PPO-Lagrangian both fail to achieve zero violation even with a zero cost limit

title: Direct Behavior Specification via Constrained Reinforcement Learning
statement: A constraint that is long to satisfy drives its multiplier very large and destabilises learning.
quote: a constraint that enforces a behavior which is long to discover can end up reaching very large multiplier values. It then leads to very large policy updates and destabilizes the learning dynamics.

title: Direct Behavior Specification via Constrained Reinforcement Learning
statement: With an impossible constraint the multiplier grows without bound and critic/performance collapse.
location: Sec. 6.1 Fig. 3; full text not accessed for this section

title: Direct Behavior Specification via Constrained Reinforcement Learning
statement: Under many constraints the reward gets almost no weight while a feasible policy is sought.
quote: leaves very little to no traction to improve on the main task while the process is looking for a feasible policy.

title: Feasible Actor-Critic: Constrained Reinforcement Learning for Ensuring Statewise Safety
statement: For infeasible states the statewise multiplier diverges to infinity under primal-dual ascent.

title: Reachability Constrained Reinforcement Learning
statement: Constraints cannot be satisfied outside the feasible set so multipliers diverge without a cap.

title: Towards Fast Safe Online Reinforcement Learning via Policy Finetuning
statement: The multiplier learned offline is orders of magnitude off the value needed online.
quote: in BallCircle, the offline Lagrange multiplier value obtained using the BEAR-lag algorithm is approximately 1500, whereas during online finetuning, the SAC-lag requires a value of only about 0.65.

title: Towards Fast Safe Online Reinforcement Learning via Policy Finetuning
statement: A mis-initialised multiplier after the shift causes violations or stagnation.
quote: Improper initialization can lead to extensive constraint violations or training stagnation, an issue we term as the Lagrange multiplier mismatch.

title: Adaptive Shielding for Safe Reinforcement Learning under Hidden-Parameter Dynamics Shifts
statement: Across hidden-parameter contexts constrained baselines cannot balance safety and return even with parameters observed.
quote: These results highlight the challenge of balancing safety and returns, even when hidden parameters are provided as inputs, in the presence of varying hidden parameters.

title: Adaptive Shielding for Safe Reinforcement Learning under Hidden-Parameter Dynamics Shifts
statement: Out-of-distribution contexts break the safety-performance trade-off of baselines.
quote: The remaining algorithms exhibit high variance and sensitivity to dynamics shifts, failing to maintain a consistent safety-performance trade-off across environments.

title: Safe Meta-Reinforcement Learning via Information Space Reachability
statement: Whether a state is safe depends on the task posterior so safety is context-dependent.
quote: safety under task uncertainty is inherently belief-dependent: the same physical state may admit different safety guarantees under different task posteriors.

title: Safe Continual Reinforcement Learning under Nonstationarity via Adaptive Safety Constraints
statement: A constraint fixed for one context stops describing safety after the context changes.
quote: First, a policy may satisfy an outdated constraint that no longer captures safety in the changed environment.

title: SPiDR: A Simple Approach for Zero-Shot Safety in Sim-to-Real Transfer
statement: Domain-randomised constrained training often violates constraints on the target dynamics.
environment: RWRL / Safety Gym / RaceCar / real robots
quote: domain randomization lacks safety guarantees and often fails to satisfy the constraints in practice (cf. Queeney and Benosman, 2024, and Figure 3).

title: SPiDR: A Simple Approach for Zero-Shot Safety in Sim-to-Real Transfer
statement: Averaging cost over randomised contexts can underestimate cost in the deployment context.
quote: since simulators only approximate the real world with limited precision, as well as due to averaging over dynamics, the costs in Equation (2) may underestimate the true costs in M*.

title: Safety Generalization Under Distribution Shift in Safe Reinforcement Learning: A Diabetes Testbed
statement: Policies that meet the constraint on the training patient violate it on unseen patients.
quote: policies satisfying constraints during training frequently violate safety requirements on unseen patients.

title: Generalizing from a few environments in safety-critical reinforcement learning
statement: Agents safe on few training levels fail catastrophically on unseen levels.
quote: We find RL algorithms can fail dangerously on unseen test environments even when performing perfectly on training environments.

title: Risk-Averse Model Uncertainty for Distributionally Robust Safe Reinforcement Learning
statement: Misspecified domain randomisation gives little safety benefit over standard safe RL under perturbation.

title: Towards a Practical Understanding of Lagrangian Methods in Safe Reinforcement Learning
statement: λ is highly sensitive and constraint restrictiveness changes with the cost limit within a task.
quote: Our results reveal the highly sensitive nature of λ and further show that the restrictiveness of the constraint cost can vary across different cost limits within the same task.

title: Evaluation Metrics for Safe Reinforcement Learning
statement: A policy within budget with exploration noise violates it when evaluated deterministically.

title: Effects of Safety State Augmentation on Safe Exploration
statement: Sparse and unknown cost gives the learner too little signal and causes violations.
quote: Often the safety cost is sparse and unknown, which unavoidably leads to constraint violations

title: Effects of Safety State Augmentation on Safe Exploration
statement: Safe action depends on cost already spent so a Markov policy without budget state fails.
quote: at the crossing of these paths robot needs to know which path it took to this state. Switching from the green path to the blue one will lead to a constraint violation.

title: Seeing Before Colliding: Anticipatory Safe RL with Frozen Vision-Language Models
statement: Cost arrives only after collision and λ only rises after the budget is exceeded.

title: BCPPO: Bachelier-Inspired Constrained Proximal Policy Optimization for Tail-Risk-Aware Safe Reinforcement Learning
statement: An expected-cost budget is met even when a rare fraction of rollouts incurs large cost.

title: SB-TRPO: Towards Safe Reinforcement Learning with Hard Constraints
statement: With zero budget the multiplier only grows and traps the policy in conservative regimes.
